D5 Friction and Efficiency in Drive Systems: practice

Booklet 5 Drive Systems · Lesson D5

What this page practises

  • I can describe the effects of friction in a drive system.
  • I can describe ways to reduce friction.
  • I can explain how to improve efficiency, with a cause and an effect.
  • I can calculate the efficiency of a system.

Warm-up

Say it the exam way

Friction is a force that motion. In a drive system, friction wastes energy as and sound, and makes the moving parts .

To reduce friction, the gears with oil or grease, fit on the shafts, or use a slippier material.

Efficiency = energy out ÷ energy . Efficiency has . No drive system is efficient.

Check your understanding

Answer in your jotter first. Then open the answer.

1. State two effects of friction in a gear train.

Show the answer

Any two: energy is lost as heat (and sound); the moving parts wear; the efficiency is lower.

2. State two ways to reduce friction in a gear train.

Show the answer

Any two: lubricate the gears (oil or grease); fit bearings; use a smoother ("slippier") material.

3. A motor gives 500 J of energy to a gear train. The gear train gives out 400 J. Calculate the efficiency.

Show the answer

efficiency = energy out ÷ energy in = 400 ÷ 500 = 0.8 (80%)

4. Explain why lubricating the gears makes the battery of a cordless drill last longer.

Show the answer

Lubricating reduces friction (cause), so less energy is lost as heat and the battery lasts longer (effect).

5. Name the part fitted to a shaft to reduce friction.

Show the answer

A bearing.

Errors that cost marks

  • No single words. "Oil" alone got no mark. Say what and where: lubricate the gears (2014, 2024).
  • "Explain" needs a cause and an effect: lubricate the gears (cause) to reduce friction, so less energy is lost (effect) (2017, 2021, 2024).
  • In 2024 the cause had to name the gear train: lubricate the gears, not just "lubricate".
  • Not 100% efficient: energy is lost as heat or sound (1 mark), due to friction (1 mark) (2015).
  • Efficiency has no unit: 0.46 or 46% (2015).

Answers

Say it the exam way

(1) opposes · (2) heat · (3) wear · (4) lubricate · (5) bearings · (6) in · (7) no unit · (8) 100%

Check your understanding

  1. Any two: energy is lost as heat (and sound); the moving parts wear; the efficiency is lower.
  2. Any two: lubricate the gears (oil or grease); fit bearings; use a smoother ("slippier") material.
  3. efficiency = energy out ÷ energy in = 400 ÷ 500 = 0.8 (80%)
  4. Lubricating reduces friction (cause), so less energy is lost as heat and the battery lasts longer (effect).
  5. A bearing.
